explainer.title: Design-and-build or construct-only?
explainer.intro: The contract type decides who is responsible for what. Both work well – it depends on how much you want to control yourself.

columns.title: Design-and-build (totalentreprenad)
columns.text: We are responsible for both design and construction. You describe what you need – function, quality and budget – and we develop the solutions.
points: One party is responsible for the whole project
Suits clients who want to hand over the details
Normally governed by the Swedish standard contract ABT

columns.title: Construct-only (utförandeentreprenad)
columns.text: You, or your architect, produce the drawings and specifications. We build to those documents and are responsible for the workmanship.
points: You control the design in detail
Suits projects where the design is already complete
Normally governed by the Swedish standard contract AB

includes: Cost estimate and fixed price based on the agreed documents

Project management and coordination of all subcontractors
Health and safety coordination (BAS-P and BAS-U) when required
Self-inspections and documentation during construction
Final inspection, as-built drawings and operation and maintenance manuals
Warranty under standard industry contracts, with a warranty inspection

process.title: Contact
process.text: You tell us about the project. We ask about needs, timeline and budget.

process.text: We look at the plot or property and go through the conditions.

process.text: We build. You have a project manager and regular check-ins.

process.title: Warranty
process.text: We fix any defects during the warranty period and carry out a warranty inspection before it ends.

faq.q: How long does it take to build?
faq.a: It depends on size, structure, permits and season. You get a schedule for your project together with the quote, and we review it continuously during construction.

faq.q: Can you help with building permits?
faq.a: Yes. We prepare the documents needed and handle contact with the municipality. The decision itself is made by the municipal building committee.

faq.q: What does the fixed price include?
faq.a: Everything in the agreed documents. Changes and additions you order during construction are priced before they are carried out, so you always know what they cost.

faq.q: Who is the certified inspector (KA)?
faq.a: Most building projects require a certified control officer (kontrollansvarig) who is independent of us as the contractor. We help you find one.

faq.q: What warranty do you give?
faq.a: We give a warranty under standard industry contracts, counted from the approved final inspection. Before the warranty ends we carry out a warranty inspection together with you.

cta.title: Planning to build?
cta.text: Tell us about the plot, the idea or the drawings you have. We will come back with a proposed approach.

process.title: Contact
process.text: You tell us what needs doing and when would suit you.

process.title: Survey
process.text: We inspect the property and review your maintenance plan, if you have one.

process.title: Quote
process.text: You get proposed measures, a schedule and a fixed price to decide on.

process.title: Execution
process.text: We inform residents and carry out the work on schedule.

process.title: Final inspection
process.text: The work is inspected and the documentation handed over.

process.title: Warranty
process.text: We fix any defects that appear during the warranty period at no cost.

faq.q: Can residents stay during pipe replacement?
faq.a: Usually yes, but for a period the bathroom and kitchen cannot be fully used. We arrange temporary facilities such as showers and toilets, and inform all residents well in advance.

faq.q: Can I get the ROT tax deduction?
faq.a: Private individuals can get a ROT deduction for the labour cost of renovating their home. We deduct the amount directly on the invoice. The rules change from time to time, so check the current rules on the Swedish Tax Agency's website.

faq.q: How do we know what needs doing?
faq.a: We start with a survey and review the maintenance plan. Then you get a prioritised proposal, so you can choose what to do now and what can wait.

faq.q: Is a building permit needed?
faq.a: Some work, such as changing the facade or converting a loft, requires a permit or notification. We find out what applies and help with the application.

faq.q: How much disruption will there be?
faq.a: It depends on the work. The schedule shows which days will be noisy or have the water or power off. Residents are informed in the stairwell and by letter in good time.

cta.title: Time to renovate?
cta.text: Tell us what needs doing. We start with a survey and give you a solid basis for your decision.

process.title: Contact
process.text: You tell us about the property and what you need help with.

process.title: Review
process.text: We go through agreements, finances and the condition of the property.

process.title: Quote
process.text: You get a proposal with a fixed price for the parts you choose.

process.title: Handover
process.text: We take over from your current manager without interrupting invoicing or payments.

process.title: Ongoing management

process.title: Follow-up
process.text: We track budget and maintenance plan and suggest improvements.

faq.q: Can we change manager in the middle of the financial year?
faq.a: Yes. We plan the handover with the board and your current manager so that invoicing, payments and bookkeeping continue without interruption.

faq.q: How often is a ventilation inspection (OVK) required?
faq.a: The interval is set by the National Board of Housing, Building and Planning and depends on the type of building and ventilation system. We keep track of when it is due, book the inspection and make sure any remarks are fixed.

faq.q: How long is an energy performance certificate valid?
faq.a: Ten years. We make sure it is renewed on time and suggest measures that lower your energy costs.

faq.q: What is a maintenance plan?
faq.a: A plan of which parts of the property need maintenance and when, often 30–50 years ahead. It is the basis for the budget and for allocations to the maintenance fund.

faq.q: Can we buy financial management only?
faq.a: Yes. Choose the parts that suit your co-op or property and add more later.

cta.title: What would management cost?

faq.q: What counts as an emergency?
faq.a: Faults that could cause injury or damage to the property if not fixed immediately – for example a water leak, a blocked drain, a power cut in the whole apartment, a break-in or a front door that will not lock.

faq.q: How quickly does the on-call team arrive?
faq.a: Emergencies always come first. When you call we assess the situation straight away and deal with anything that can't wait as quickly as possible – less urgent jobs are scheduled into regular maintenance.

faq.q: Can we order snow clearing separately?
faq.a: Yes. Snow clearing and gritting can be agreed for the season, with or without other caretaking.

faq.q: How do we follow up on what has been done?
faq.a: Every job is logged with date and action. You get a summary as often as we agree and can always ask your contact person.

faq.q: Which decisions must be taken at the general meeting?
faq.a: It depends on the work and your co-op's statutes. Major renovations that affect members' apartments may require a decision at a general meeting, sometimes by a qualified majority. We help you find out what applies before you proceed.

faq.q: Can you take over from our current manager?
faq.a: Yes. We plan the handover with the board and your current manager so fees and payments continue as normal.

faq.q: How are members kept informed during a renovation?
faq.a: Through notices in the stairwell, letters and information meetings when needed. Members learn what will be done, when it affects them and who to contact.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: It depends on the size of the co-op and what you need. After a first meeting you receive a quote with a fixed price for management and separate prices for any projects.

faq.q: What counts as an emergency?
faq.a: Faults that could cause injury or damage to the property if not fixed immediately – for example a water leak, a blocked drain, a power cut in the whole apartment, a break-in or a front door that will not lock. Call us straight away on {phone}.

faq.q: When will my fault be fixed?
faq.a: You get a confirmation once we have received your report. Non-urgent faults are normally fixed within a few working days. We will let you know if it takes longer, for example if parts need ordering.

faq.q: Can you enter my apartment when I am not home?
faq.a: Only if you have given permission in your fault report. Otherwise we will contact you to book a time.

faq.q: Who is responsible for what in the apartment?
faq.a: The landlord is responsible for the building and its fixed equipment. As a tenant you are responsible for taking care of the apartment and reporting faults. In a co-operative apartment, you as a member are responsible for interior maintenance according to the co-op's statutes.

faq.q: Can I sublet my apartment?
faq.a: You need to apply and get approval before the subletting starts. Use the form under Forms.

faq.q: How do I give notice on my apartment?
faq.a: Notice must be given in writing. Use the form under Forms or send a signed letter. The notice period for a rental apartment is normally three months unless otherwise agreed.

forms.title: Forms
forms.text: Download and fill in the form, then send it to us using the contact form or give it to your caretaker. The forms are in Swedish – contact us if you need help.

rules.title: House rules
rules.intro: A few simple rules help everyone enjoy living here. The full rules are in your lease or the co-op's statutes.

items.title: Be considerate
items.text: Keep noise down in the evening and at night, especially between 10 pm and 7 am.

items.title: Laundry room
items.text: Book a time, stick to it and clean up after yourself.

items.title: Waste and recycling
items.text: Sort into the right bins. Bulky and electrical waste goes to the municipality's recycling centre.

items.title: Stairwell
items.text: Do not leave things in the stairwell. It is an escape route and must be kept clear.

items.title: Balconies and barbecues
items.text: Electric and gas barbecues are fine on balconies and patios. Be considerate about smoke and smells.

items.title: Smoking
items.text: Smoking is not allowed in stairwells, the laundry room or other shared spaces.

in.title: Moving in
items: Arrange electricity and home insurance before you move in.
Collect your keys – we agree on a time and place once the lease is signed.
Check the apartment and report any faults within a week.
Register your change of address with the Swedish Tax Agency.
Order a name plate for the door and letterbox through the fault report form.

out.title: Moving out
items: Give notice in writing. The notice period is normally three months.
We book a move-out inspection with you.
Clean the apartment, storage room and any garage.
Return all keys – we book a time for the handover together with the inspection.
Register your change of address with the Swedish Tax Agency.

about.h1: A local company, responsible all the way
about.lead: We build, renovate and manage properties in {serviceArea}.

story.title: Who we are
body: Solrik is a Skåne-based property management and construction company and part of Radiant Group. We look after housing cooperatives and property owners throughout a building’s life – from day-to-day management and maintenance to renovation and new construction.

What sets us apart is that the same organisation manages, maintains and builds. The people planning the maintenance know what the work costs to carry out, and the people renovating know how the building will be looked after afterwards. For you, that means fewer handovers, clearer responsibility and one contact who knows the property.

items.title: Responsibility
items.text: We take responsibility for the whole job, including what our subcontractors do. What is in the contract applies, and what we promise, we deliver.

items.title: Quality
items.text: Done right the first time. We document our work with self-inspections and hand over a property that is easy to look after.

items.title: Proximity
items.text: We work where we live. Short distances mean quick answers, and residents should recognise the people who come.

sustainability.title: Sustainability
sustainability.intro: Building and property management affect the environment and people for a long time. This is how we work.

items.title: Energy efficiency
items.text: We propose measures that reduce energy use – insulation, ventilation with heat recovery and better heating controls. Every proposal is costed, so you can see both the saving and the payback time.

items.title: Choice of materials
items.text: We choose durable materials and document them for future maintenance. Where possible we reuse materials instead of buying new.

items.title: Waste sorting
items.text: Construction waste is sorted on site into the required fractions, including wood, metal, plastic, plasterboard, glass and mineral waste. That cuts both the environmental impact and the cost of waste handling.

items.title: Safe working environment
items.text: Everyone should get home safely. We carry out risk assessments, draw up a work environment plan and act as safety coordinator (BAS-P and BAS-U) when required. A tidy, well-run site is part of the job.

list: Quote requests – to reply and provide a quote. Legal basis: legitimate interest and steps prior to a contract.
Fault reports – to fix the fault. Legal basis: performance of a contract, such as a lease or management agreement.
Customers and contracts – to perform the contract and invoice. Legal basis: contract.
Bookkeeping – to comply with the Swedish Bookkeeping Act. Legal basis: legal obligation.
Job applications – to handle recruitment. Legal basis: legitimate interest.

sections.title: How long we keep the data
list: Quote requests that do not lead to a contract: twelve months.
Fault reports: two years after the case is closed.
Contracts and invoices: seven years under the Bookkeeping Act.
Job applications: six months after the recruitment ends.

sections.title: Who we share data with
body: We never sell your data. We only share it when needed to carry out the work, for example with:
list: tradespeople and subcontractors fixing a fault or carrying out an assignment
the property owner or housing co-op we manage for
providers of IT and form handling ({formProvider}) who process data on our behalf

sections.title: Transfers outside the EU/EEA
body: Some IT providers may process data outside the EU/EEA, for example in the USA. We then make sure the transfer is supported by the GDPR, for example through the European Commission's standard contractual clauses or because the recipient is certified under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You have the right to:
list: find out what data we hold about you
have data erased when it is no longer needed
receive data you have provided in a machine-readable format (data portability)
after: Call us on {phone} or write to us using the contact form to exercise your rights.

sections.title: Complaints
body: If you are unhappy with how we process your personal data, you can complain to the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY), imy.se.

sections.title: Cookies
body: Information about cookies is on our cookies page.

sections.title: Changes
body: We may update this policy. The latest version is always available here.
